userPrompt: A running task can be paused and resumed. A Pause button beside Cancel stops the harness's run, leaving the task in the history as "Paused", its output, conversation, and starting snapshot kept. A paused task offers Resume, which carries on the same task, not a new one: it continues the task's conversation, telling the harness that its run was interrupted, that any step it was in the middle of may not have finished, and that files may have changed since, so it checks what it needs before carrying on from where it left off rather than starting over. The task's output continues beneath what it had, its time counts only while it runs, and its changed files and diff span the whole task, from the snapshot taken when it first started to the one taken when it finally ends. While a task is paused, its lane's queue carries on with the next prompt; a resumed task takes its place in the queue as a task sent at the time it was first sent. A paused Chain step resumes as that step, and the chain continues after it as ever. A task also pauses this way, rather than failing, when it stops because the harness's usage limit was reached.

- [A task under way is cancelled from a Cancel button; its run is stopped, its process ended](.claude/reference/scope/prompt-mode/sending/index.md#cancelling)
- [A cancelled task keeps its output and reads "Cancelled"; its lane's queue carries on after it](.claude/reference/scope/prompt-mode/sending/index.md#cancelling)
- [Each lane carries on its own conversation; a conversation is only carried on by the harness it began with](.claude/reference/scope/harness-integration/index.md#context)
- [Changed files are the diff between snapshots taken as a task started and ended](.claude/reference/scope/prompt-mode/message-list/index.md#changed-files)
- [Elapsed time counts while a task is under way and stops once it's over](.claude/reference/scope/prompt-mode/message-list/index.md#elapsed)
- [The header's Stop button cancels the task while it's under way](.claude/reference/scope/prompt-mode/message-list/index.md#buttons)
- [A chain step is sent once the step before it finishes, queued by when its chain was sent](.claude/reference/scope/prompt-mode/index.md#chained-tasks)
- [A failed run says what went wrong in the harness's own words](.claude/reference/scope/harness-integration/index.md#failures)
EOF
f=spec/scope/prompt-mode/sending/index.pi; e=$(awk 'NR>121 && /^    [a-zA-Z]+:/ {print NR; exit}' $f); head -$((e-1)) $f > /tmp/x; cat >> /tmp/x <<'EOF'
    pausing:
        A running task can be paused and resumed. A Pause button, a small
        ghost button with a pause icon, whose tooltip says "Pause this
        task", sits beside Cancel wherever Cancel does, shown while the task
        is running. Pausing stops the harness's run, its process ended as
        cancelling ends it, and leaves the task in the history as "Paused":
        its output, its conversation, and the snapshot taken as it first
        started are kept, and nothing it changed is undone. A paused task is
        not under way: its lane is free, and its queue carries on with the
        next prompt, as after any task.

        A paused task offers Resume, a small ghost button with a play icon,
        in place of Pause, wherever its actions are. Resume carries on the
        same task, never a new one: it is not saved in the history again and
        keeps its name. It carries on the task's own conversation, as the
        @{HarnessIntegration} says, with a message telling the harness that
        its run was interrupted, that any step it was in the middle of may
        not have finished, and that files may have changed since, so it
        checks what it needs before carrying on from where it left off rather
        than starting over. The message is the application's own, from the
        @{ModeSystemPrompts}, not the user's, and it is not compiled as a
        prompt; the spec is not built again ahead of it. A resumed task takes
        its place in its lane's queue as a task sent at the time it was first
        sent: it runs as soon as its lane is free, ahead of every prompt sent
        after it was first sent.

        While it is paused, its status reads "Paused", its time stops, and
        it is listed among the previous tasks, or, for a chain step, with its
        chain. Once resumed, its output carries on beneath what it had, a
        muted row marking where it was paused and resumed, its time counts on
        from where it stopped, counting only while it runs, and its changed
        files and their diffs span the whole task, from the snapshot taken
        when it first started to the one taken when it finally ends. It can
        be paused and resumed any number of times, and cancelled while
        paused, which ends it as Cancelled. A paused task whose conversation
        can no longer be carried on resumes as a new conversation, as the
        @{HarnessIntegration} says, told the task's prompt and its output so
        far.

        A paused Chain step resumes as that step, and the chain carries on
        after it as ever, its next step sent once it finishes. While one of
        its steps is paused and none runs, the chain reads Paused.

        A task also pauses this way, rather than failing, when it stops
        because the harness's usage limit was reached, as the harness says
        in its result or its errors: it reads "Paused" with a muted note
        saying the usage limit was reached and when it resets, if the harness
        says, and waits to be resumed by hand. Paused tasks are kept across
        restarts and can be resumed after one.

EOF
tail -n +$e $f >> /tmp/x; cp /tmp/x $f
for a in HarnessIntegration ModeSystemPrompts; do grep -q "import.*\b$a\b" $f || echo "need $a"; done; grep -n "^from" $f | head -20

content.text:
Running tasks can now be paused and resumed. `piton check` reports no problems and `piton build` wrote 84 files.

- **Pause** (`.claude/reference/scope/prompt-mode/sending/index.md#pausing`): a Pause button sits next to Cancel. It ends the harness's run and leaves the task as "Paused", keeping its output, conversation and starting snapshot. Its lane's queue moves on to the next prompt.
- **Resume:** it carries on the same task, not a new one.
  - **The message it sends:** it continues the task's conversation with a resume message saying the run was interrupted, that a step may not have finished and files may have changed, so check before carrying on.
  - **Queue place:** it rejoins its lane's queue at its original send time.
  - **Output:** a muted marker shows where it paused, and new output carries on beneath it.
  - **Time:** it only counts while running.
  - **Changed files:** they span from the first snapshot to the final one.
- **Pausing again or cancelling:** a task can be paused any number of times, and cancelling a paused task ends it as Cancelled.
- **If the conversation is gone:** it resumes as a new conversation, given the prompt and the output so far. That fallback is my addition.
- **Chains:** a paused step resumes as itself and the chain carries on after it. While a step is paused and none is running, the chain reads Paused.
- **Usage limit:** hitting the harness's usage limit pauses the task instead of failing it, with a note giving when the limit resets.
- **Across restarts:** paused tasks survive restarts.
- **Where it shows:**
  - A "Paused" status label in the warning colour.
  - Pause and Resume buttons in the task header and the Tasks tab's actions.
  - An editable `resume.md` prompt with a default text, alongside the project's other prompts.
